Definition: Ability to centrally monitor and manage compute, storage, and network resources within the HCI platform through a single, integrated interface.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No centralized visibility, infrastructure components are managed separately with limited monitoring.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic centralized dashboard exists, but visibility is limited and not all components are integrated.
Level 3 - Defined: Unified management platform provides visibility across most infrastructure components with standard monitoring.
Level 4 - Managed: Comprehensive visibility across compute, storage, and network with proactive monitoring and alerting.
Level 5 - Optimized: End-to-end visibility across environments (including hybrid/multi-site) with advanced analytics and capacity insights.

Definition: Ability to plan, execute, and manage software and firmware updates (hypervisor, storage, firmware, and HCI stack) in a coordinated and controlled manner across the infrastructure.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Updates are performed manually and inconsistently across components with no standard process.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic update procedures exist, but patching is still fragmented and requires multiple tools or manual coordination.
Level 3 - Defined: Standardized patching and upgrade processes are in place with planned schedules and documented procedures.
Level 4 - Managed: Upgrades are centrally managed and coordinated across the HCI stack with minimal disruption and consistent execution.
Level 5 - Optimized: Lifecycle management is streamlined and regularly executed with minimal downtime, ensuring systems remain up-to-date and stable.

Definition: Effectiveness of managing and operating HCI infrastructure in terms of time, effort, resource utilization, and consistency of execution.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Operations are manual, time-consuming, and inconsistent, leading to frequent delays and inefficiencies.
Level 2 - Developing: Some processes are streamlined, but operations still require significant manual effort and coordination.
Level 3 - Defined: Standard operating procedures are established, improving consistency but still dependent on manual execution.
Level 4 - Managed: Operations are efficient with reduced manual effort, supported by standardized processes and better resource utilization.
Level 5 - Optimized: Operations are highly efficient with minimal overhead, continuously improved to maximize productivity and performance.

Definition: Ability to monitor, forecast, and plan infrastructure capacity using real-time and historical data, ensuring resources are available proactively rather than reacting to shortages.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No capacity planning, resources are added only after performance issues or shortages occur.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic capacity tracking exists, but planning is reactive and based on limited or manual data.
Level 3 - Defined: Capacity planning is performed periodically using historical trends, with defined thresholds for key resources.
Level 4 - Managed: Capacity is continuously monitored with alerts and proactive planning aligned to growth and demand patterns.
Level 5 - Optimized: Capacity planning is integrated into operations using real-time insights, ensuring timely scaling and efficient resource utilization.

Definition: Ability of the HCI infrastructure to deliver consistent and predictable improvements in performance and capacity when resources (nodes, storage, compute) are added, without introducing bottlenecks.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Scaling is unplanned, adding resources does not consistently improve performance and may create bottlenecks.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic scaling is possible, but performance gains are inconsistent due to configuration or architectural limitations.
Level 3 - Defined: Scaling processes are defined, capacity increases are predictable, but performance improvements vary across workloads.
Level 4 - Managed: Scaling is tested and predictable, adding resources improves both capacity and performance for most workloads.
Level 5 - Optimized: Scaling consistently delivers expected performance gains across workloads with minimal bottlenecks.

Definition: Effectiveness of utilizing compute and storage resources within the HCI environment to balance performance and capacity without over- or under-provisioning.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No visibility into resource usage, frequent over- or under-provisioning leads to inefficiency and performance issues.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic utilization monitoring exists, but resource allocation is not optimized and often manually adjusted.
Level 3 - Defined: Utilization is monitored with defined thresholds, resources are allocated based on standard practices, but not fully optimized.
Level 4 - Managed: Resources are efficiently utilized with proactive monitoring and adjustments to balance performance and capacity.
Level 5 - Optimized: Resource utilization is continuously optimized based on workload needs, maximizing efficiency while maintaining performance.

Definition: Ability of the HCI platform to protect data using built-in features such as snapshots and replication (local and remote) to ensure data availability and recoverability.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No consistent use of native data protection features, reliance is mainly on external backups.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic snapshots or replication are configured for select workloads, but coverage is limited and inconsistent.
Level 3 - Defined: Snapshots and replication are implemented for critical workloads with defined policies, but not fully standardized.
Level 4 - Managed: Data protection features are consistently applied across workloads with regular monitoring and policy enforcement.
Level 5 - Optimized: Snapshots and replication are fully integrated into operations, providing reliable and efficient data protection across environments.

Definition: Extent to which the HCI platform is integrated with backup solutions and the percentage of workloads consistently protected by backup policies.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Backups are not consistently configured, many workloads are unprotected and integration with backup tools is minimal.
Level 2 - Developing: Backups are implemented for critical workloads only, integration exists but coverage is partial and inconsistent.
Level 3 - Defined: Backup solution is integrated with HCI platform, most workloads are protected with defined policies.
Level 4 - Managed: Backup coverage is comprehensive with consistent policy enforcement and reliable integration across environments.
Level 5 - Optimized: All workloads are protected with standardized policies, backup integration is seamless and regularly validated.

Definition: Ability to protect backup and snapshot data from ransomware attacks using mechanisms such as immutability, access controls, and isolated storage to ensure clean recovery.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No specific ransomware protection, backups and data can be modified or deleted, making them vulnerable to attacks.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic security controls (e.g., access restrictions) are in place, but data is still modifiable and exposed.
Level 3 - Defined: Secure backup repositories and controlled access are implemented, but immutability is limited or not consistently enforced.
Level 4 - Managed: Immutable backups or storage (e.g. WORM/object lock) are enabled with strict access controls to prevent modification or deletion.
Level 5 - Optimized: Immutable and/or isolated (air-gapped) backups are in place with regular validation to ensure reliable recovery from ransomware incidents.

Definition: Ability of the HCI environment to meet defined Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) and Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) through appropriate data protection replication and recovery processes.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No defined RPO/RTO, recovery capabilities are unclear and not aligned with business needs.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic RPO/RTO targets exist for some critical workloads, but are not consistently met.
Level 3 - Defined: RPO/RTO are defined for key systems with supporting backup or replication, but execution is inconsistent.
Level 4 - Managed: RPO/RTO targets are consistently achieved for critical workloads through tested DR processes.
Level 5 - Optimized: DR capabilities are well-aligned with business requirements, recovery is reliable and consistently meets defined RPO/RTO across environments.
